key_insight: Grow the Harness learns recurring agent control as reusable code, so the LLM focuses on task-specific reasoning instead of rebuilding the same strategy in every prompt.
engineering_relevance: This can sharply cut inference cost and model calls while keeping agent performance stable across smaller deployment models.
method: Start from a strategy-free scaffold with fixed model/tool interfaces but no built-in controller.
Use function-level execution traces to localize failures, then repair a small code window jointly.
Keep accepted edits in one shared harness, with a held-out success gate to roll back harmful changes.
evidence_signal: Across BrowseComp-Plus and WebArena-Verified with 4B to 120B models, the method achieved the best mean success in 5 of 6 settings and reduced LLM calls by 76.0–91.8%.
watch_item: Because the harness itself evolves from feedback, careful rollback and validation are needed to avoid accumulating brittle or task-specific control logic.
paper_title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
